add.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia)
add.summary: Federal placement policy applicable to trans prisoners in federal custody inside Saskatchewan: since 2018 the Correctional Service of Canada accommodates offenders based on gender identity rather than sex assigned at birth and permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement in a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression regardless of anatomy or identity-document sex/gender marker, refusing requests individually only where 'overriding health or safety concerns' cannot be resolved; as of 2025, of 90 self-identified transgender women in federal custody, 73 were housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's. The Office of the Correctional Investigator (2022-23 report) welcomed the 2022 gender-diversity policy but flagged unclear override parameters and the absence of a dedicated mechanism for gender-diverse prisoners to report abuse; provincial correctional policies vary (the article's only provincial example is Ontario) and no Saskatchewan-specific rule or case is documented in this source.
